citation: Menne, Matthew J., and Claude N. Williams Jr. (2009). Homogenization of Temperature Series via Pairwise Comparisons. Journal of Climate 22(7): 1700-1717.
verification_status: verified primary DOI metadata and NOAA copy
formal_problem: Detect and adjust artificial station-series inhomogeneities through pairwise differences.
inputs: Monthly station series, neighboring station network, and station history when available.
assumptions: Neighbor comparisons expose local artificial breaks and some shift magnitudes can be reliably estimated.
ground_truth: Simulated step/trend scenarios and real U.S. temperature observations; no complete verified historical transition ledger.
local_common_distinction: Operationally distinguishes a station-attributed break from shared climate variation, but does not define the proposed three-state event task.
physical_control_independence: No independent physical control; neighbors are comparison references.
synthetic_real_truth_separation: Partial: simulations impose known changes while real observations lack complete event truth.
missing_negative_evidence: Not formalized as missing evidence versus negative evidence.
exact_metashift_overlap: Network comparison, weak history/metadata, and measurement-break attribution.
exact_unresolved_gap: No formal criterion for weakly anchored event identifiability, explicit answer risk-coverage, or abstention policy.
novelty_effect: Narrows any claim that network pairwise detection or metadata use is novel.

citation: Williams, Claude N. Jr., Matthew J. Menne, and Peter W. Thorne (2012). Benchmarking the performance of pairwise homogenization of surface temperatures in the United States. Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres 117: D05116.
verification_status: verified primary bibliographic record and canonical university repository
formal_problem: Benchmark pairwise homogenization accuracy and uncertainty using realistic temperature analogs.
inputs: Perturbed homogenization ensembles, benchmark analogs of real monthly temperature series, and real observations.
assumptions: Benchmark analog construction represents relevant systematic errors.
ground_truth: Known benchmark truth; real-world truth remains unavailable.
metadata_anchors: Uses PHA context, not a formal weak-anchor identifiability analysis.
synthetic_real_truth_separation: Yes: benchmark truth is separated from real-data inference.
risk_coverage: Error bounds on trends, not selective answered-event risk plus coverage.
exact_metashift_overlap: Realistic synthetic benchmarking and incomplete real-world truth.
exact_unresolved_gap: No individual weak-anchor identifiability criterion, decision rule requiring abstention, or complete event accounting.
novelty_effect: Narrows novelty of realistic injected-truth benchmarking and synthetic/real truth separation.

citation: Barigozzi, Matteo, Haeran Cho, and Piotr Fryzlewicz (2018). Simultaneous multiple change-point and factor analysis for high-dimensional time series. Journal of Econometrics 206(1): 187-225.
formal_problem: Locate multiple second-order change-points and assign common or idiosyncratic factor-model origin.
inputs: High-dimensional time-series panel, approximate factor model, and wavelet transforms.
assumptions: Piecewise stationarity and approximate factor-model structure.
ground_truth: Known simulated changes; empirical applications do not provide a complete event-truth ledger.
local_common_distinction: Yes; common and idiosyncratic components are central, including possible idiosyncratic-to-common spillover.
physical_control_independence: No; factor components are statistical rather than physically independent controls.
synthetic_real_truth_separation: Simulation/application distinction exists but not a measurement-transition truth protocol.
exact_unresolved_gap: No weak metadata anchors, physical measurement-transition setting, complete event universe, answer-risk/coverage, or abstention policy.
novelty_effect: Strongly narrows any claim that common/idiosyncratic distinction itself is novel.

citation: Taiebat, Morteza, and Farrokh Sassani (2017). Distinguishing Sensor Faults from System Faults by Utilizing Minimum Sensor Redundancy. Transactions of the Canadian Society for Mechanical Engineering 41(3): 469-487.
verification_status: verified publisher DOI, author record, title, venue, volume, issue, and pages
formal_problem: Distinguish sensor faults from system faults using minimum sensor redundancy.
inputs: Sensor observations, number of sensors/variables, and known physical relationships.
assumptions: Serial causality, serially connected systems, and sufficient sensor redundancy.
ground_truth: Controlled reservoir/control-valve demonstration, not historical network-event labels.
local_common_distinction: Analogous sensor-versus-system distinction, not statistical common/idiosyncratic network change-points.
physical_control_independence: Yes; known physical relationships and redundancy are essential.
synthetic_real_truth_separation: Controlled demonstration is separate from historical deployment.
risk_coverage: Conditional certainty result, not an answered-case risk-coverage curve.
exact_unresolved_gap: Its certainty result needs strong physical structure and does not cover weak anchors, historical-event completeness, selective event decisions, or post-selection uncertainty.
novelty_effect: Most important restriction: do not claim generic novelty for conditional identifiability or sensor/system distinction.

citation: Abadie, Alberto (2021). Using Synthetic Controls: Feasibility, Data Requirements, and Methodological Aspects. Journal of Economic Literature 59(2): 391-425.
formal_problem: Estimate counterfactual treatment effects with weighted donor units and assess design feasibility.
inputs: Treated-unit outcomes, donor outcomes, pre-treatment covariates, and outcomes.
assumptions: Donors approximate an untreated trajectory with suitable data, design, and pre-treatment fit.
ground_truth: The untreated counterfactual is unobserved; placebos are diagnostics rather than labels.
local_common_distinction: Treated-versus-donor comparison, not local-versus-common measurement-transition classification.
physical_control_independence: Donor pool is a comparator, not independently controlled physical instrumentation.
synthetic_real_truth_separation: Not a central synthetic-event/real-event truth separation protocol.
risk_coverage: Inference and diagnostics, not answered-event risk plus coverage.
explicit_abstention: No formal abstention, although feasibility failures are discussed.
exact_metashift_overlap: Counterfactual comparison, pre-fit feasibility, and placebo logic.
exact_unresolved_gap: No weak-anchor transition identifiability, selective decision rule, or complete event universe.
novelty_effect: Narrows novelty of counterfactual comparison, feasibility checks, and placebo diagnostics.

citation: El-Yaniv, Ran, and Yair Wiener (2010). On the Foundations of Noise-free Selective Classification. Journal of Machine Learning Research 11: 1605-1641.
formal_problem: Characterize and optimize selective-classification risk-coverage trade-offs.
inputs: Labeled examples, classifier, and selection/reject rule.
assumptions: Noise-free classification models for the main theory.
complete_event_universe: Not applicable to historical event enumeration.
exact_metashift_overlap: Answered-case error/risk and coverage with rejection.
exact_unresolved_gap: No network-event identifiability, weak anchors, physical controls, or event-universe design.
novelty_effect: Narrows novelty of risk-coverage and abstention.

citation: Geifman, Yonatan, and Ran El-Yaniv (2017). Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks. NeurIPS 2017.
verification_status: verified canonical preprint and proceedings record
formal_problem: Construct a selective deep classifier that targets a prescribed risk with high probability.
inputs: Trained DNN, confidence score, and labeled calibration/training data.
assumptions: IID labeled data and a confidence score that ranks reliability.
ground_truth: Fully labeled CIFAR and ImageNet benchmarks.
risk_coverage: Yes; selective risk and coverage with a risk target.
post_selection_uncertainty: Controls accepted-case risk, not selection-conditional interval coverage.
exact_metashift_overlap: Explicit answer-versus-abstain operationalization and answered-case risk control.
exact_unresolved_gap: No weak operational anchors, event identifiability, monitoring network, or complete event universe.
novelty_effect: Narrows novelty of target-risk abstention mechanisms.

citation: Cauchois, Maxime, Suyash Gupta, Alnur Ali, and John C. Duchi (2024). Predictive Inference with Weak Supervision. Journal of Machine Learning Research 25(118): 1-45.
formal_problem: Construct distribution-free predictive confidence sets from partial or weak labels.
inputs: Features plus a weak label or weak-labeling function.
assumptions: Weak labels encode a set containing the true label and conformal assumptions apply; strong-label coverage is generally impossible without more assumptions.
ground_truth: Weak labels and experiments, not a complete measurement-event truth ledger.
metadata_anchors: Weak-labeling functions are mathematical supervision objects, not operational metadata anchors.
risk_coverage: Coverage for a weak-label-consistent set, not selective answered-event risk plus coverage.
explicit_abstention: Set-valued prediction, not a prescribed abstention policy.
missing_negative_evidence: Recognizes unobserved strong labels but not missing-log versus negative-event-evidence semantics.
exact_metashift_overlap: Weak supervision, impossibility under insufficient information, and valid uncertainty.
exact_unresolved_gap: No network measurement-transition identification, local/common structure, or required abstention.
novelty_effect: Narrows novelty of weak-supervision validity or impossibility reasoning.

citation: Angelopoulos, Anastasios N., Stephen Bates, Adam Fisch, Lihua Lei, and Tal Schuster (2024). Conformal Risk Control. ICLR 2024.
verification_status: verified canonical OpenReview record and bibliographic metadata
formal_problem: Control expected monotone losses with conformal calibration.
inputs: Calibration data, predictor, and monotone loss.
assumptions: Conformal calibration assumptions with extensions for selected shifts.
risk_coverage: Expected-risk control, not a risk-coverage event-identification framework.
exact_metashift_overlap: Risk-control component potentially relevant to answered claims.
exact_unresolved_gap: No network measurement-event identification, weak anchoring, or abstention requirement.
novelty_effect: Narrows a generic claim of novelty for conformal expected-risk control.

citation: Jin, Ying, and Zhimei Ren (2025). Confidence on the Focal: Conformal Prediction with Selection-Conditional Coverage. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 87(4): 1239-1259.
verification_status: verified primary DOI metadata and canonical preprint
formal_problem: Construct prediction sets with exact coverage conditional on data-driven focal-unit selection.
inputs: Calibration data, test covariates, selection rule, and conformity scores.
assumptions: Exchangeability and specified permutation-invariance conditions for selection.
ground_truth: Observed labels/outcomes for calibration and prediction targets with unknown outcomes.
risk_coverage: Conditional coverage for selected focal units, not an event risk-coverage frontier.
explicit_abstention: Selection is modeled; abstention is not its object.
exact_unresolved_gap: No weak operational anchors, monitoring-network structure, or event-cause identifiability.
novelty_effect: Directly narrows novelty of post-selection uncertainty conditional on selection.

citation: van den Burg, Gerrit J. J., and Christopher K. I. Williams (2020). An Evaluation of Change Point Detection Algorithms. arXiv:2003.06222.
verification_status: verified canonical arXiv record and Alan Turing Institute project record
formal_problem: Benchmark change-point detectors when real-world truth is uncertain.
inputs: Thirty-seven real time series, five human annotations per series, and candidate detectors.
assumptions: Human annotations are imperfect references and multiple annotations need dedicated metrics.
ground_truth: Five expert annotations per real series, with explicitly uncertain real-world ground truth.
complete_event_universe: No complete objective event universe; labels are annotations.
synthetic_real_truth_separation: Yes in a broad sense; acknowledges uncertainty in real truth and evaluates it explicitly.
missing_negative_evidence: Does not frame missing logs versus negative evidence.
exact_metashift_overlap: Benchmarking under unavailable or ambiguous real ground truth.
exact_unresolved_gap: No weak-anchor identifiability, physical controls, answer-risk/coverage, or abstention decision policy.
novelty_effect: Narrows a generic claim that incomplete real ground truth alone makes benchmark design novel.

citation: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. About AQS Data; AQS Manuals and Guides; Federal Reference and Equivalent Method guidance.
formal_problem: Document public air-quality measurements, site/equipment metadata, and associated QA data.
inputs: AQS measurements, site/equipment metadata, QA data, API services, and public data files.
assumptions: Monitoring/reporting requirements, submission schedules, resubmissions, and time-varying coverage.
ground_truth: Administrative and measurement records, not complete historical event labels.
metadata_anchors: Yes; metadata can locate candidates but does not determine mechanism.
physical_control_independence: No independent physical control status is supplied by the documentation.
complete_event_universe: No; an enumeration rule must be separately defined.
missing_negative_evidence: Missing metadata is not proof that no event occurred.
exact_metashift_overlap: Public measurement/metadata provenance and comparability context.
exact_unresolved_gap: Does not establish causal mechanism, physical fault, complete historical labels, or independent-network validation.
novelty_effect: Constrains the meaning of anchors and any claim of complete event enumeration.

citation: Le Cam, Lucien (1986). Asymptotic Methods in Statistical Decision Theory. Springer Series in Statistics.
verification_status: verified Crossref bibliographic record and Springer DOI
formal_problem: Formalize statistical experiments, decision risk, and limits imposed by observational equivalence.
inputs: Probability laws, decision rules, losses, priors, and experiments.
assumptions: Claims depend on the explicitly specified experiment, distributional assumptions, and loss.
ground_truth: Theoretical laws, not a measurement-event truth ledger.
local_common_distinction: Provides the statistical-experiment language for equal observation laws, not a local/common monitoring construction.
exact_unresolved_gap: Observational equivalence and decision-theoretic lower-bound framing.
novelty_effect: No weak anchors, monitoring network, physical-site constraints, complete event accounting, or empirical auditing policy.
column23: Requires the project to state its equivalence propositions as elementary scoped benchmark contracts rather than unprecedented theory.
